findings.description: Critical: The MODIFIED Profile-Aware Setup requirement adds "SHALL NOT import agent-coordinator source modules" (spec.md:12) while retaining the Local profile setup scenario step that registers MCP "with env vars from get_mcp_env()" (spec.md:20). get_mcp_env() is an agent-coordinator API; satisfying that THEN clause requires the import the same requirement forbids. Portable Skill Payload (spec.md:157) repeats the ban. Design D3 keeps MCP registration as narrated make targets, which is also incompatible with naming get_mcp_env(). An implementer following the scenario literally produces an illegal dependency; following D3/Portable leaves the MODIFIED scenario unmet.
findings.resolution: Rewrite Local profile setup step 4 to the public surface the skill already uses (e.g. make -C "$COORDINATOR_DIR" mcp-setup / documented coordinator setup targets). Remove the get_mcp_env() reference. Clarify which Local/Railway steps remain SKILL.md narration versus script subcommands so the MODIFIED preamble and D3 stay aligned.

findings.description: Critical: Design D2 says to follow skills/refresh-architecture/scripts/arch_utils/provenance.py:43-55 "exactly" for the guarded atomic import fallback. That precedent's except-branch _atomic_write_bytes (provenance.py:55-61) is target.write_bytes(payload) — not tmp+fsync+os.replace. Atomic Permission Allowlist / Concurrent reader safety (spec.md:116-117, 142-145) require a temporary file replaced into place with no partial reads, with no carve-out for the unbundled path. Portable Skill Payload (spec.md:159-160, Sibling skill unavailable) makes the fallback a supported production path. Following D2 "exactly" reintroduces defect #3 (non-atomic write) precisely when project-context-runtime is absent.
findings.resolution: Keep the guarded import of atomic_write_bytes, but define an inline fallback that still does same-directory tempfile + flush/fsync + os.replace + parent fsync (the durability the design rejected copying only to avoid duplication). Update D2 to state that the precedent is the import wiring, not the non-atomic fallback body. Add a test that with the import forced to fail, configure still performs an atomic replace.

findings.description: Critical: harness-report.schema.json admits state=ready with config_artifact=null and config_present=true (Draft202012Validator reports 0 errors for that document). Spec Harness Presence Detection defines ready as "CLI present and config artifact present" (spec.md:81) and D5/unknown semantics treat a null artifact as unknown, not ready. The ready if/then branch only const-checks cli_on_path and config_present (schema lines 117-124), so the wp-core "Entrypoint --json output validates against the contract" gate can green-light an incoherent report that the spec forbids.
findings.resolution: Extend the ready if/then branch to require config_artifact as a non-empty string (and keep config_present const true). Mirror the config_missing branch's artifact constraint. Add a negative schema test fixture for ready+null artifact.

findings.description: Nit: Design D7 and work-packages prescribe settings-writer cases as xfail-on-legacy / pass-on-new, and wp-core verifies with `pytest ... -k legacy` under the name "Legacy shim still exhibits all four defects". skills/ has no xfail_strict (confirmed absent from pyproject/pytest config). Under pytest 9 defaults, an unexpectedly passing xfail (XPASS) exits 0 — reproduced locally — so if the shim stops exhibiting a defect, the gate still passes. That is the same class of self-defeating gate the iterate pass already called out elsewhere.
findings.resolution: Prefer positive assertions of defective legacy behavior (assert the deny-list false positive still occurs) rather than xfail on the corrected behavior; or set xfail(strict=True) on legacy params and assert the gate fails on XPASS. Name/parametrize with stable ids containing "legacy" so -k legacy cannot silently deselect.

findings.description: Nit: Script-Backed Entrypoint requires binary exit codes "0 when the requested state is satisfied, non-zero when it is not" (spec.md:59) but never defines the satisfied state for detect-harnesses (or report). Presence reporting can succeed while every vendor is cli_missing. Task 3.1 covers "exit-code discipline" without pinning whether mixed/non-ready reports are exit 0 or non-zero, so two conforming implementations diverge and the contract gate only checks JSON shape.
findings.resolution: Add an explicit SHALL: detect-harnesses exits 0 when a roster was resolved and a report emitted (presence check succeeded), independent of per-vendor state; reserve non-zero for resolve failures / usage errors. State the analogous rule for report/check/configure.

findings.description: Nit: After MODIFIED merge, Local profile setup and Railway profile setup scenarios (spec.md:14-31) still list docker auto-start, MCP registration, curl health, and coordination_bridge detect as unconditional skill SHALLs, but tasks 3.6–3.8 only implement profile resolution, settings configure, and capability report, and D3 keeps make mcp-setup/hooks-setup as narration. No task maps those orchestration steps to an automated test. As written, the scenarios are either untestable obligations on markdown or silent scope creep into the entrypoint.
findings.resolution: Split each scenario into script-backed THEN clauses (check/report/configure) versus narrated operator steps (compose up, make mcp-setup, bridge detect), or move the orchestration bullets under a non-normative note so validate-feature/playwright-style checks are not implied.

findings.description: Optional: Task 3.7 implements report with no preceding failing-test task (unlike detect-harnesses, settings writer, and CLI dispatch). Profile-Aware Setup still requires capability-flag reporting, so report can land unpinned except for manual checkpoints.
findings.resolution: Add a small red-test task before 3.7 asserting transport/CAN_* summary shape for --json and human output, or explicitly mark report as covered by extending task 3.1's CLI contract tests.

findings.description: The intentional write_allow overlap on skills/tests/setup-coordinator/test_skill_md.py between wp-core (tests/setup-coordinator/**) and wp-integration is sound: packages are strictly sequential via depends_on, and wp-integration's description forbids wp-core from creating that file. Combined with D1a/D1b matching vendor_health.load_agents_yaml (lines 110-155) and the live agents.yaml roster (seven cli agents including claude-remote/codex-remote), the core detection plan is grounded in repository reality rather than assumed APIs.

Design D2's correction to call atomic_write_bytes rather than atomic_write_json is accurately grounded: canonical_json_bytes in atomic.py:31-40 uses sort_keys=True, and the live .claude/settings.local.json top-level order is [permissions, disabledMcpjsonServers], so canonicalization would both reformat unrelated keys and defeat idempotent no-op detection. Requiring that seam is the highest-value plan correction from the iterate pass.
